title: CMMC Level 1 Readiness Check
line: 15 questions, one for each Level 1 requirement. About five minutes.
honest: A self-check. Your answers stay on this device and nobody else sees them. It is not the Level 1 self-assessment the rule asks you to post, and it is not an assessment by anyone else.

items.question: Is access to your systems limited to authorized users, to processes acting for them, and to authorized devices?
items.next: List who and what may use each system, and remove every account and device that is not on the list.

items.question: Is each user limited to the kinds of transactions and functions that user is permitted to carry out?
items.next: Give each account only the functions its user needs, and take administrator rights off everyday accounts.

items.question: Do you verify and control connections to systems outside your own, and limit how they are used?
items.next: List the outside systems and services you connect to, and decide which are allowed for contract information.

items.question: Do you control what is posted or processed on systems the public can reach?
items.next: Name who may post to your public sites, and review what is there for contract information.

items.question: Can you identify every user, every process acting for a user and every device on your systems?
items.next: Give each person, service account and device an identifier of its own; end shared accounts.

items.question: Do you authenticate, or verify, each of those identities before allowing access?
items.next: Require every account and device to authenticate before it reaches your systems.

items.question: Do you sanitize or destroy media that held federal contract information before you dispose of it or release it for reuse?
items.next: Wipe or destroy drives, phones and paper before disposal or reuse, and keep a record that you did.

items.question: Is physical access to your systems, your equipment and the rooms they run in limited to authorized people?
items.next: Lock the rooms and the equipment, and list who is authorized to enter.

items.question: Do you escort visitors and watch what they do, keep logs of physical access, and control keys, badges and other access devices?
items.next: Start a visitor log, escort every visitor, and account for every key and badge.

items.question: Do you monitor, control and protect communications at the outer boundary of your systems and at key boundaries inside them?
items.next: Put a firewall at the boundary, and review what it lets in and out.

items.question: Are the parts of your systems the public can reach on a subnetwork separated from your internal networks?
items.next: Move public-facing servers onto a separate network segment.

items.question: Do you identify, report and correct flaws in your systems in a timely manner?
items.next: Turn on updates, and set a time limit for applying security patches.

items.question: Is there protection from malicious code at the appropriate places in your systems?
items.next: Run protection from malicious code on every computer and at the mail gateway.

items.question: Do you update that protection when new releases are available?
items.next: Set the protection from malicious code to update itself.

items.question: Do you scan your systems periodically, and scan files from outside sources as they are downloaded, opened or run?
items.next: Schedule periodic scans, and turn on real-time scanning of files from outside.
